_doc: Cheap-mode knobs for job-search-and-apply. Copied to memory/career/config.json during setup. The skill reads this file at the start of every run; edit it any time, no restart needed.
_applications_per_run: How many applications one run produces. 2 fits a $20 Claude plan's 5-hour message window. Raise to 5+ on a larger plan.
_stagger_minutes: Gap between application sessions. The first starts immediately; each later one is scheduled this many minutes after the previous, so usage spreads across the day instead of draining the window at once. Set 0 to run them all in parallel.
_model: Model for both the search session and the application sessions. Sonnet is roughly a fifth the cost of Opus per message and fills forms just as well. Only move to Opus if tailoring quality is visibly suffering.
_search_mode: "script" runs tools/find_jobs.py against job-board APIs and gives the model a ranked shortlist — much cheaper, because the model never reads raw job-board pages. "model" lets the agent search the web itself: better at odd or local employers, several times the cost.
_candidate_multiplier: Shortlist size = applications_per_run x this. Cutting from a wider pool is what makes the picks good; the script does the widening, so it costs almost nothing.
_write_cover_letters: false = write one only when the form makes it mandatory. Long prose is the most expensive output there is and rarely changes the outcome.
_max_free_text_words: Ceiling on any single free-text answer unless the form states a longer minimum. Keeps screening answers short and cheap.
_search_keywords: Words find_jobs.py ranks on. Job titles work best — "test engineer", "controls engineer". A hit in the posting title scores 5x a hit in the body. Filled from profile.md targets during setup.
_search_cities: Location strings that count as commutable, e.g. ["Los Angeles", "Long Beach", "Irvine"]. Matched against the posting's location text, so list the actual city names rather than a radius.
_min_salary: Annual floor. Only filters postings that state a number; ones that say nothing still come through, because a silent posting is worth reading. 0 disables it.
_remote_ok: Whether remote postings get a ranking boost.
_target_companies: Optional. Employers to check every run regardless of keyword match. Their job boards live in tools/boards.json, which is what find_jobs.py actually queries. Workday and Taleo employers have no open API — the agent searches those directly.
_auto_submit: true = the application session submits once every field is filled and checked. false = it fills everything, stops before the submit button, and flags the session for you to press it. Start with false for the first few if you want to watch it work.
_quiet_hours: No application session is scheduled to start inside this window, local time.
